Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex Medical Devices Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Thompson, CEO; Lisa Chen, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Mark Reynolds, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Medical Devices had a productive Q3, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
2. Competitive dynamics and market share trends
3. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
4. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
5. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
6. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

Lisa will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Patel will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with our overall performance highlights and key achievements.

I'm thrilled with how we executed this quarter, delivering net revenues of $1.32 billion, up 18% year-over-year on a reported basis and 19% on a constant currency basis. This extends our streak to 11 straight quarters of double-digit organic growth, well ahead of the broader medtech market's 7-9% pace as tracked by PwC and Evaluate MedTech. Strength came across all core segments, powered by surging procedure volumes, market share gains, and steady pricing.

In cardiovascular solutions, our biggest unit at 52% of revenues, we hit $665 million, surging 22% year-over-year. TAVR procedures jumped 25% globally, thanks to our next-gen ApexFlow Harmony valve grabbing an extra 3.2 points of U.S. market share to 28% in low-risk patients, pulling ahead of rivals like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien line. Electrophysiology also shone with our RhythmSync ablation system securing 15% average selling price growth from AI-guided mapping capabilities, echoing Boston Scientific's Farapulse momentum.

Structural heart and endovascular added 28% of revenues at $370 million, up 16%, buoyed by more aortic aneurysm repairs in an aging population. Our Zenith Flex AAA stent graft earned a CE Mark renewal in Europe, sparking 30% growth there. Diagnostics and monitoring rounded it out at 20% or $265 million, up 12%, led by 1.2 million units shipped of our CardioWatch Pro wearable—a 40% rise—taking share in remote monitoring much like Abbott's FreeStyle Libre setup. EHR integration via FHIR standards drove 45% growth in recurring SaaS revenues.

Adjusted EBITDA margins widened 210 basis points to 32.4%, fueled by $85 million in gross margin gains from supply chain tweaks like 15% lower resin costs via Southeast Asian dual-sourcing and shifting balloon catheter production stateside. Free cash flow reached $420 million, funding $250 million in share repurchases and hiking our dividend to $0.45 per share.

Regionally, growth was balanced: U.S. at $810 million or 61% of total, up 17%, aided by CMS IPPS updates equalizing TAVR reimbursements and 20% procedure volume gains in ambulatory surgery centers. EMEA hit $330 million, up 24% reported and 27% constant currency, our top performer thanks to UK NHS uptake and German HTA nods. APAC reached $140 million, up 14%, with China now 12% of the mix after NMPA clearance for ApexFlow Harmony, offset by brief COVID flares. Emerging markets like LATAM contributed $40 million, soaring 30% through Brazilian and Mexican distributor ramps.

Key milestones this quarter spotlight our innovation and agility: FDA PMA approval for the PulseFlow pulsatile pump in LVAD therapy opens a $2.5 billion market growing 12% annually, complementing Medtronic's HeartWare and prepping 2025 rollouts. At TCT 2024, we debuted our AI-Enhanced Imaging Suite with generative AI for real-time 3D intravascular ultrasound, trimming procedure times 22% in early tests. R&D spend hit 12.5% of revenues at $165 million, with 45% going to digital therapeutics and robotics, including pilots for our RoboCath system challenging da Vinci.

Strategically, we sealed a $1.1 billion deal for NeuroVasc Solutions, beefing up neurovascular stents against Penumbra and Stryker. A co-development with Siemens Healthineers on hybrid OR imaging eyes $300 million in synergies by 2027. U.S. cardiovascular share now at 14.5% per NPM data, up from 12.8% last year. On sustainability, Scope 3 emissions dropped 25% via recycled nitinol, meeting EU MDR rules, while our MedTech Secure program neutralized 95% of cyber threats.

These wins reinforce our Innovate, Expand, Execute strategy. We're lifting full-year 2024 guidance to $5.25-$5.35 billion in revenues, 17-19% growth, and 32-33% EBITDA margins, with Q4 EPS at $1.90-$2.00. Procedurals stay strong in a $150 billion-plus TAM expanding 8% on pent-up demand and value-based care.

Now, let's talk about competitive dynamics and market share trends.

Our positioning in structural heart and neuromodulation remains robust as the global structural heart market eyes 12-15% CAGR to 2028, propelled by demographics, TAVR/mitral/LAAO volume surges, and Level 1A trial data. Neuromodulation for renal denervation in hypertension and spinal cord stim for pain grows 9-11%, with better reimbursements and real-world proof.

Globally, structural heart share hit 22.3% in Q3, up 210 basis points year-over-year per IQVIA and Millennium-aligned tracking—six quarters running of gains versus 11.2% market growth. Neuromodulation held 18.7%, plus 90 basis points, led by RenalDenerv RF snagging 25% of new hypertension cases.

The landscape is fragmented yet consolidating. Edwards Lifesciences leads U.S. TAVR at ~45% with Sapien 3 Ultra and Evolut FX, but yielded 1.5 points in mitral/tricuspid to our TriFlow clip and TriGuard valve, boasting better 12-month durability from TRILUMINATE Pivotal. Medtronic's CoreValve Evolut at 28% TAVR lags our AccuValve delivery system's 18% vascular complication drop in ACCELERATE registry, driving 14% uptake in big centers. Abbott's Amplatzer Amulet at 32% LAAO lost 3 points to our Watchman FLX Pro at 22%, via FOREVER labeling for tricky anatomies.

In neuromodulation, Boston Scientific's Vercise DBS and Symplicity Spyral at ~35% combined face our SympaThick multi-electrode array at 22% in tough hypertension, with SPYRAL HTN-ON MED data showing 32 mmHg systolic drop at 36 months—better longevity.

By region: U.S. (62% revenue) structural heart share to 24.1%, up 280 bps, on CMS low-risk TAVR parity and 15% ASP lifts from IDN deals like Kaiser/HCA; we took 65% new Northeast TAVR starts amid 13% volumes. Europe (22%) up 150 bps to 19.8% despite rival CE delays; TriFlow's July MDR win sped German/French mitral at 16% growth. APAC (12%) stellar, China to 16.5% post-AccuValve NMPA, riding 25% procedures; emerging LATAM/India up 28% organically with low-cost EchoGuard LAAO.

Shaping factors: $450 million R&D yielded three IDEs, like ValveNav AI imaging cutting fluoro time 27% for robotics akin to da Vinci's heart push. Pricing steady at $32,500 U.S. TAVR amid bundles, 8% Europe premium on data. Supply localization—40% catheters in Mexico—beat 12% inflation peers like Stryker saw.

We're pursuing tuck-ins like $1.2 billion NeuroPulse adding 5% neuromod share, Siemens 4D CT partnerships, and tricuspid repair trials ($5B TAM by 2030). Expect 100-150 bps more structural heart share FY24 on 85% U.S. TAVR penetration and China doubling; 1,200+ publications and 95% physician NPS fuel 200 bps yearly gains.

Moving on to gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

Our gross margins reflect portfolio strength and operations discipline. Q3 non-GAAP gross margin was 67.2%, up 150 basis points sequentially from Q2's 65.7% and 320 basis points year-over-year—our 10th straight expansion quarter, trailing 12-month at 66.8%. GAAP at 65.9% after a $12 million inventory step-up from acquiring NeuroVasc Solutions' intracranial stent tech.

Drivers: Product mix gave 80 basis points—structural heart/neuromod like EvoFlow TAVR and PulseStim DBS leads up 28%, 42% of revenue; ortho AI Triad knees at 15% U.S. share shifted 12% to premium robotics (ASPs $18,500 TAVR kits vs. $9,200 pacemakers). Pricing discipline added 60 basis points: U.S. IDN renewals with HCA/Kaiser mid-single-digits on 22% lower EvoFlow readmits vs. Medtronic CoreValve; ex-U.S., Europe NICE pressures down 3-4% offset by 7% Brazil/India hikes. Cost efficiencies 70 basis points: Gen-3 automation in Galway, Ireland cut cardio labor 11%; $45 million resin reformulation savings in peripheral catheters using bio-polymers, holding ISO 13485 and 2 PPM defects.

Regional: U.S. 69.5% on domestic/GPO leverage; EMEA 64.2% on €0.15 titanium inflation from Ukraine but 5% robotics volumes; APAC 66.8% on 35% China VisionPro OCT despite 8% yen FX.

Ahead, FY24 gross margin to 67-68% from prior 66.5-67.5%; 2025 target 68.5-69.5% on $1.2 billion neuromod capacity and 55% 'precision medtech' shift like Helix stim at 85% scale margins.

Supply chain stabilized, Supplier Risk Index to 92/100 from Q2's 84 across 1,200 vendors. Headwinds: chip lead times 28 weeks (20% over pre-pandemic) for 8% electrophys like Boston Scientific Rhythmia; nitinol +14% from Indonesia curbs, 90 bps vascular hit; sterile packaging +9% like Abbott Libre resins.

Mitigations: Dual/multi-sourcing 92% criticals (from 75%), Vietnam/U.S. nitinol dropping single-source <5%. Nearshored 25% ortho to Reynosa, Mexico—40% lead times down, 22% transport savings, gamma sterilization dodging EtO EPA rules. Vertical integration: in-house Triad anodization cut titanium 60%, $150 million Austin silicon carbide fab vs. TSMC shortages. AI Supply Chain Control Tower with SAP Ariba/IBM Watson hit 96% forecast accuracy, $180 million excess inventory cut, safety stock to 9 weeks.

Regional delivery: U.S. 98%, Europe 91% despite Red Sea (12% delays), APAC 89% post-China lockdowns, India Vizir endoscopy ramp. Partnerships: Stryker logistics MOU for robotics, $200 million DuPont PEEK offtake.

Our Resilient MedTech 2027 roadmap targets $500 million savings for bioresorbables/closed-loop neuromod—20-25% premiums over Edwards Sapien. Margins outperform peers like Zimmer Biomet's 62-64%.

Next, the impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

These efforts countered CMS cuts on structural heart and tough GPO talks, driving margin expansion and EPS growth across cardio, ortho, neuromod.

Pricing netted 2.8% full-year ASP growth, beating 1-2% guide. Value-based models shifted 25% U.S. TAVR to outcome-linked IDN bundles (HCA/Kaiser) on readmits/survival, like Edwards Sapien—holding $32,000 ASPs up 1.5%, +12% adoption. Premium ortho robotics to 18% revenues (from 12%), +150 bps ASPs vs. 1% commodity deflation from Vizient.

Regions: U.S. (55%) flat to +1% despite 2.3% CMS DRG ICD cuts; EMEA -1.2% German HTA on neuromod leads like Medtronic InterStim, offset UK NHS 8%; APAC +5.1% China NMPA neuromod vs. MicroPort.

Costs saved $285 million FY, beating $250 million—gross margins +220 bps to 69.2%, op margins +310 bps to 28.4%. Supply/procurement $140 million via Zero-Based: renegotiated platinum-iridium/polymers for stents/leads (-4.2% materials amid 15-20% rare earths/resins inflation), 30% non-implants to Mexico/Vietnam (-18% logistics, Red Sea dodge like Intuitive).

Manufacturing: Galway/Plymouth Lean Six Sigma $95 million—22% stent cycle cuts via laser welding, +15% throughput, yields 98.7% from 96.2%. OpEx: SG&A -180 bps to 19.1% on 12% commercial headcount trim, AI sales analytics -8% reps/+ close rates on Watchman LAAO.

Tailored to med device shifts: pricing vs. UK NICE/US IRA 2026; savings fund $120 million structural heart R&D vs. Boston Watchman FLX. 7% global volumes (IQVIA) amplify 1% ASP with 10-15% electrophys growth.

FY24: 2-3% ASP, $200-250 million costs for 4-6% core growth, 10-12% EPS. Beats Abbott's 65% devices margins.

Then, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

SG&A is key at ~28% costs, sales-heavy for structural heart/neuromod/ortho like EvoFlow TAVR, Abbott Infinity DBS-like stims, da Vinci-competing robotics.

Q3 SG&A $355 million, +2% YoY absolute but -210 bps to 27.1% of sales from 29.2%—fourth straight deleveraging, $42 million op margin add. TTM 27.8%, -320 bps from Q3 2023. Ex-$15 million EU MDR charge, adjusted 26.5%.

Selling (55%) down 1% to $195 million: U.S. field sales -8% to 1,700 reps via attrition/IDN/ASC redeploy; Salesforce Einstein/OR analytics +22% productivity, +15% procedures sans travel. T&E -18% to $29 million, 65% virtual like Stryker Mako.

G&A flat $105 million: ZBB year two $25 million savings—AWS ERP consolidated IT -35%; Manila shared services (payroll/AP/AR) -40% vs. U.S. like Medtronic.

Regions: U.S. (62%) -250 bps to 26.8% on CMS EvoFlow +7% ASPs, Vizient GPOs. Europe (22%) +3% to €88 million on MDR but Dublin hub -180 bps. APAC (12%) -5% local on Japan rep cuts pre-neurostim launch, Boston Emblem-like partnerships.

Savings reinvest: $65 million YTD—40% ortho digital (patient apps/joint registries), 30% FDA PMA neuromod. FY25 target 100-150 bps deleveraging via AI CRM phase 2, ortho tuck-in synergies like Abbott NeuroPace. Aims 28% op margins amid China tariffs/U.S. reimbursement flux.

Market resilience at 5.2% CAGR to 2028 (Evaluate MedTech)—turning costs to moats.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

For Q4 2024, we guide total revenue $1.38 billion to $1.42 billion, 12-15% YoY growth at midpoint (from Q3 $1.32 billion, +4-6% sequential). Leader in structural heart/neuromod with ApexFlow TAVR gaining vs. Edwards Sapien/Medtronic Evolut, NeuroPulse DBS for Parkinson's/tremor with AI leads like Medtronic but optimized.

Segments: Structural heart (45% Q3 mix) 18-20% YoY to $630-650 million on U.S. +15% volumes post-COVID, full approval ApexFlow Ultra (better radial force/lower PVL); ASPs ~$32,000 +2% on GPO value pricing. Neuromod (30%) 10-12% to $420-440 million on depression indications like Boston Vercise, +25% int'l rechargeable IPGs. Capital/other (robotic cath labs vs. Intuitive Ion) flat to +3% at $330-340 million; hospitals capex cautious but $2.1 billion backlog +22% YoY.

Regions: U.S. (65%) 13-16% on volumes/Medicare 2.7% TAVR IPPS bump. EMEA (20%) 8-10% CC on CE renewals/Germany/UK gains, MDR delays hit smaller foes. APAC (10%) 15-18% China ApexFlow NMPA to $100 million run-rate mid-2025, 1-2% U.S.-China tariff drag. ROW (5%) double-digits LATAM/India low-cost stents.

Margins: non-GAAP gross 68.5-69.5%, +150 bps from Q3 67.2% on high-margin disposables (72% revenue), Guadalajara Mexico efficiencies -8% logistics on vascular kits, +100 bps pricing vs. platinum-iridium inflation. Op margin 24.5-25.5% from Q3 23.1% on $25 million SG&A digital AI sales (rep +18%); R&D 12% revenue for Phase III bioresorbable scaffold FDA H1 2025.

FY2025 revenue raised to $5.65-$5.85 billion, 11-14% organic over FY24 ~$5.1 billion: mid-teens structural heart on demographics (500K annual TAVR by 2030 iRhythm-like), double-digit neuromod +$200 million wearables PulseSync app/Apple Health like Abbott NeuroSphere. Conservative capex, M&A upside post-$450 million RhythmTech (electrophys).

FY25 gross 69-70% on 787i components/Singapore automation vs. 50 bps USD FX; op 25.5-26.5%, EPS $4.85-$5.05 at 25% tax, $1.2 billion buybacks.

Risks: hospital staffing caps low-end volumes, CMS structural bundling, rare earths MRI disruptions. Upside: China CRO real-world studies, ortho OX-7 knee recapture. Confident via pipeline (3 Q1 IDEs), #2 U.S. TAVR 22% share (Definiti), execution in 7-9% CAGR market (Grand View).

I will now turn the call over to Lisa for a review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. As David highlighted so comprehensively, we delivered solid financial performance this quarter, with revenues up 18% to $1.32 billion, gross margins expanding to 67.2%, and strong free cash flow supporting capital returns. Expenses were well-controlled, with SG&A deleveraging meaningfully and operating margins climbing toward our targets. Profitability metrics exceeded expectations, and our balance sheet remains rock-solid with $2.5 billion in cash and low leverage.

For Q4 and FY2025, we're guiding as David outlined: revenues $1.38-1.42 billion for Q4 and $5.65-5.85 billion full year, with gross margins 68.5-69.5% and op margins 24.5-25.5% this quarter, scaling higher next year. These reflect our mix shift, pricing actions, and efficiencies across the board.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for ApexFlow Ultra, which is showing promising results in reducing paravalvular leak rates and improving radial force, positioning us strongly against competitors.

Our pipeline is robust, with Phase III data for the bioresorbable scaffold on track for FDA submission H1 2025, and early success in closed-loop neuromodulation for depression and hypertension. We've secured three IDE approvals expected Q1, including AI-enhanced ValveNav for structural heart robotics integration. Wearables like PulseSync are integrating seamlessly with ecosystems like Apple Health for remote monitoring, driving $200 million incremental opportunity. Investments at 12.5% of revenue are fueling innovations like RoboCath and Helix stimulator, targeting 20-25% margin premiums. Real-world evidence studies with China CROs and U.S. registries like ACCELERATE underscore our data leadership.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. David, on the Q4 revenue guide and FY25 raise, can you expand on the China ramp assumptions for ApexFlow and any tariff mitigations?

David Thompson:
Thanks, Alex. Absolutely, the China piece is a key driver in APAC's 15-18% growth guide. Post-NMPA, we're targeting $100 million annualized run-rate by mid-2025, partnering with local CROs for real-world evidence to accelerate adoption amid 25% procedural surges. Tariffs are a 1-2% headwind on components, but we've derisked via nearshoring 30% production to Vietnam/Mexico and dual-sourcing nitinol—our Supplier Risk Index at 92/100 ensures resilience. Overall, mid-teens structural heart growth assumes demographic tailwinds like 500K annual TAVR procedures by 2030. Confident in the midpoint.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Great, thanks. Lisa, gross margins hit 67.2%—impressive expansion. Can you detail the supply chain levers sustaining this into 2025, especially semiconductors and EtO?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Emily. Yes, mix shift to 72% high-margin disposables like ApexFlow kits contributed 80 bps, pricing 60 bps, and costs 70 bps from Galway automation and bio-resin reformulations. Supply-wise, chip lead times at 28 weeks for 8% of portfolio are managed with multi-sourcing at 92% coverage and our Austin silicon fab ramp. For EtO, Reynosa's gamma irradiation qualifies 25% ortho nearshoring, cutting leads 40%. AI Control Tower forecast accuracy at 96% trimmed inventory $180 million. FY25 69-70% on scale and automation—outpacing peers despite 5-7% raw mat inflation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Thanks. Mark, on competitive dynamics, how are you gaining share in EMEA structural heart amid MDR, and APAC outlook?

Mark Reynolds:
Hi Mike. In EMEA, up 150 bps to 19.8% share despite delays hitting smaller players—our TriFlow got full MDR in July, driving 16% mitral growth in Germany/France on superior TRILUMINATE durability vs. Edwards. NHS UK frameworks added momentum. APAC's the star: China share to 16.5% post-AccuValve NMPA on 25% volumes; India/LATAM +28% with EchoGuard low-cost LAAO. U.S. 24.1% on IDN value contracts. Innovation like ValveNav AI (27% less fluoro) and 95% NPS keep us gaining 200 bps annually. Targeting tricuspid $5B TAM next.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
Thanks. Raj, exciting pipeline. Details on Helix neurostim and bioresorbable scaffold timelines, integration with wearables?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thanks, Sarah. Helix, our precision neuromod for depression/hypertension, boasts 85% scale margins via multi-electrode like SympaThick—SPYRAL data shows 32 mmHg BP drop at 36 months. Phase III on track, depression indications expanding like Vercise. Bioresorbable scaffold Phase III wraps for H1 2025 FDA—aims premium over Sapien. Wearables PulseSync syncs Apple Health/EHRs for remote monitoring, +$200 million FY25; 1.2 million CardioWatch units shipped, 45% SaaS recurring. Three Q1 IDEs include PulseFlow LVAD pump. R&D 12.5% funds this for 12-15% CAGR leadership.

David Thompson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
